- **Vertex Position Instability:** Optimization of vertex positions is unstable, especially as the mesh becomes more subdivided and tetrahedra get smaller, increasing the chance of inversion [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that vertex position optimization is unstable, particularly as the mesh becomes more subdivided and tetrahedra get smaller, which increases the chance of inversion. Source [S1] explicitly confirms this in Section 9 (Discussion and Conclusion), stating: 'The optimization of vertex positions using the presented technique has proven to be quite unstable. This gets worse the more subdivided the mesh becomes. As tetrahedra get smaller, the chance of inversion increases.' Additionally, Section 8.2 notes that optimization is only stable at very low learning rates and produces lower PSNR compared to color-only optimization, further supporting the instability claim.
